hints: Focus on which functional groups actually react with sodium, remember both alcohols and carboxylic acids give hydrogen with Na.
Count the number of -OH and -CO2H groups in each of the four structures to check statement 1.
Classify each alcohol as primary, secondary or tertiary by counting carbons attached to the C-OH carbon, then see if statements 2 and 3 hold.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1 - reaction with sodium**

Sodium reacts with any O-H that is acidic enough. That means alcohols and carboxylic acids, but not aldehydes or ketones.

$$\text{ROH + Na} \rightarrow \text{RONa + } \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2$$
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H + Na} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{Na + } \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2$$

**Count reactive groups in each isomer**

$\text{HOCH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OH}$ has 2 x alcohol OH. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$ has 2 x alcohol OH, aldehyde does not react. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ has 1 x alcohol OH + 1 x acid OH. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ has 1 x alcohol OH + 1 x acid OH.

Each has exactly two reactive H atoms, so 1 mol reacts with 2 mol Na. Statement 1 is correct.

**Classify the alcohols for statements 2 and 3**

Primary is $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$, secondary is $\text{R}_2\text{CHOH}$, tertiary is $\text{R}_3\text{COH}$.

$\text{HOCH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OH}$: two primary. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$: one primary + one secondary. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$: one primary. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$: one secondary only.

**Conclude**

No isomer has a tertiary alcohol, so statement 2 is false. The last isomer, lactic acid, has no primary alcohol, so statement 3 is false. Only statement 1 is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 fails because none of the four has a tertiary alcohol, and statement 3 fails because CH3CH(OH)CO2H has only a secondary alcohol.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is wrong. Check each C-OH: all are CH2OH (primary) or CH(OH) (secondary). There is no C with three carbons attached to the C-OH.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean statements 2 and 3 are correct. Both are false. There are zero tertiary alcohols, not one, and the lactic acid isomer CH3CH(OH)CO2H contains no primary HOCH2 group.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 is correct. Each isomer has exactly two Na-reactive protons (2x OH, or 1x OH + 1x CO2H), so 1 mol needs 2 mol Na. Statements 2 and 3 are false as shown by alcohol classification.
